lessons.title: Greetings

words.meaning: A friendly way to greet someone.
What you say when you leave.
A polite word when you ask for something.
What you say when someone helps you.
What you say when you make a mistake.

listen: Hello, my name is Anna. Nice to meet you.
Good morning. How are you today?
speak: Hello, nice to meet you.
Thank you very much.

grammar.title: Verb to be: am, is, are
grammar.rule: I am, you are, he is. The verb to be links you to a word that describes you.

quiz.prompt: Complete: I ___ happy to meet you.
Which is polite when you ask for something?

lessons.title: Introductions

words.meaning: Used to say where you started.
The work you do for money.
To see someone for the first time.

listen: Hi, I am Marco. I am from Italy and I live in London.
What do you do? I am a nurse.
speak: My name is Sam and I am from Delhi.
I live in a small city.

grammar.title: Present simple for facts
grammar.rule: Use present simple for things that are always true. Add -s for he, she and it.

lessons.title: Numbers and time

words.meaning: Used to say the exact hour.
words.example: The class starts at nine o'clock.
I wake up at half past six.

listen: The train leaves at half past seven, so be at the station at seven.
The shop opens at nine and closes at eight.
speak: I start work at nine o'clock.
The meeting is at half past two.

grammar.title: Prepositions of time: at, on, in
grammar.rule: At for clock time, on for days, in for months and years.

quiz.prompt: Complete: I have a meeting ___ Friday.

lessons.title: Family

words.meaning: A male child of your parents.
A female child of your parents.

words.example: She is married to a doctor.
We visit our relatives in summer.

listen: There are four people in my family: my parents, my sister and me.
My brother has two children, so I am an uncle.
speak: I have one brother and two sisters.
My parents live in another city.

grammar.title: Have and has
grammar.rule: Use have with I, you, we and they. Use has with he, she and it.

lessons.title: At the restaurant

words.meaning: The list of food a restaurant has.
words.example: Can I see the menu, please?

words.meaning: To ask for the food you want.
words.example: I would like to order now.

words.meaning: The paper that shows what you must pay.
The person who serves your food.

words.example: I have a reservation for two.

listen: Good evening. Do you have a reservation?
I would like to order a pizza and a glass of water, please.
speak: I would like to order a pizza.
Could we have the bill, please?

grammar.title: I would like
grammar.rule: I would like is a polite way to say I want. Use it with a noun or with to plus a verb.
examples: I would like to order now.

options: I like to order pizza now.
I would like to order pizza.
quiz.explanation: Would like takes to plus the verb.

quiz.prompt: What do you ask for when you want to pay?
quiz.explanation: The bill shows what you owe.
Would is always followed by the base verb.

lessons.title: Shopping

words.meaning: How big or small something is.
words.example: Do you have a bigger size?

words.meaning: The paper that proves you paid.

listen: That is twenty-five euros. Will you pay by card or cash?
Sorry, we do not have that size in blue.
speak: How much does this cost?
Do you have this in a smaller size?

grammar.title: How much and how many
grammar.rule: How much for things you cannot count, how many for things you can.
examples: How many bags do you need?
How much time do we have?

lessons.title: Getting around

words.meaning: The paper that lets you travel.
Where you wait for a train.
words.example: The train leaves from platform three.
Go straight for two hundred metres.

listen: Go straight, then turn right at the traffic lights. The station is on your left.
The next train to the airport leaves from platform two in ten minutes.
speak: Excuse me, where is the station?
Is there a bank nearby?

grammar.title: Imperatives for directions
grammar.rule: Use the base verb with no subject to give instructions.

quiz.explanation: Instructions use the base verb alone.

quiz.prompt: Complete: The train leaves ___ platform four.
Which word means close to here?

lessons.title: At home

words.example: The kitchen is small but bright.

words.meaning: Money you pay to live somewhere.
words.example: The rent is due on the first.
I tidy my room on Sunday.

words.meaning: A person who lives next to you.

listen: The flat has two bedrooms, a small kitchen and a balcony.
I clean the house on Saturday morning and rest in the afternoon.
speak: I live in a small flat with two rooms.
My neighbour helps me a lot.

grammar.title: There is and there are
grammar.rule: There is for one thing, there are for more than one.
examples: There is a table in the kitchen.

quiz.prompt: Complete: ___ three rooms in my flat.
Complete: ___ a problem with the water.
Which word has no plural form?

lessons.title: My daily routine

words.example: I usually wake up at six.

words.meaning: The first meal of the day.
words.example: I skip breakfast on busy days.

words.meaning: The things you do every day.

listen: I usually get up at six thirty, have breakfast, and leave home before eight.
On Sundays I rarely set an alarm.
speak: I usually wake up at seven o'clock.
I rarely go out during the week.

grammar.title: Adverbs of frequency
grammar.rule: Always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never go before the main verb but after to be.

options: I go by bus always go.
quiz.explanation: Frequency adverbs go before the main verb.
After to be the adverb comes second.

lessons.title: Last weekend

words.meaning: Went to see a person or place.

words.example: I stayed at home all day.
I was tired after the trip.

listen: Last weekend I visited my cousins. We ate too much and watched an old film.
On Sunday I stayed home because I was tired.
speak: Last weekend I visited my family.
Yesterday I watched a good film.

grammar.title: Past simple
grammar.rule: Regular verbs add -ed. Common verbs are irregular: go becomes went, eat becomes ate.

options: Yesterday I go to the market.
Yesterday I went to the market.

quiz.prompt: Complete: We ___ not see the film.
quiz.explanation: Did not plus the base verb.

quiz.prompt: What is the past of eat?

lessons.title: Making plans

words.example: Let us meet up at six.
Maybe we can go on Sunday.

listen: Are you free tomorrow evening? We are going to try the new cafe.
I will let you know by tonight.
speak: I am going to visit my friend tomorrow.
Are you free on Saturday evening?

grammar.title: Will and going to
grammar.rule: Will for a decision now, going to for a plan you already made.
examples: I am going to start a course.
We are going to move in June.

quiz.prompt: You already booked tickets. You say:
options: I am going to travel on Friday.
quiz.explanation: A made plan uses going to.

quiz.prompt: The phone rings and you decide to answer. You say:
options: I am going to get it.

lessons.title: Weather and small talk

words.meaning: Hot and wet in the air.

listen: It looks cloudy today, and the forecast says rain after lunch.
Yesterday was freezing, but tomorrow will be warmer.
speak: It is very humid today.
The forecast says it will rain tomorrow.

grammar.title: It is for weather
grammar.rule: Weather sentences start with it, even though nothing is doing the action.

quiz.explanation: The forecast is it, so the verb takes -s.

lessons.title: Asking for help

words.meaning: To make something easier for someone.
words.example: Could you help me with this bag?

words.meaning: To hold something and move it.
words.example: I cannot carry all of these.

words.meaning: To make something clear to someone.

words.example: Could you repeat the last word?

listen: Excuse me, could you help me? I am looking for platform four.
Sorry, could you say that again more slowly? I did not catch it.
speak: Could you help me, please?
Sorry, could you repeat that?

grammar.title: Polite requests with could and can
grammar.rule: Can you is fine with friends. Could you is safer with strangers. Both take the base verb.

quiz.prompt: Which is more polite to a stranger?
quiz.explanation: Could you is the polite form.

lessons.title: Making an appointment

words.meaning: A particular day of a month.

words.example: I booked a table for eight.

words.meaning: To organise a time or a plan.
words.example: Let us arrange a time to talk.

words.meaning: To move something to a later date.
words.example: We put off the meeting until Monday.

listen: Good morning. I would like to book an appointment for next week if possible.
Thursday at four is open. Shall I put you down for that?
speak: I would like to book an appointment.
Does Thursday afternoon suit you?

grammar.title: Yes or no questions with be and do
grammar.rule: Put am, is or are first with be. Put do or does first with other verbs.

quiz.prompt: Complete: ___ he have time on Friday?
Which phrase means to move something to a later date?

lessons.title: Saying sorry

words.example: It was my mistake, not yours.
I forgot to send the message.

words.meaning: To say you will certainly do something.
words.example: I promise it will not happen again.
I understand why you are upset.

listen: I am really sorry. I forgot to call you back yesterday and I should have.
That is alright. It happens. Let us find another time.
speak: I am sorry, it was my mistake.
I forgot to tell you, and I apologise.

grammar.title: Past simple of irregular verbs
grammar.rule: Many common verbs do not add -ed. Forget becomes forgot, tell becomes told, say becomes said.

quiz.prompt: What is the past of forget?
Which word means responsibility for something bad?

lessons.title: On the phone

words.example: I will call back after lunch.

words.meaning: Written or spoken information you leave.
words.example: She left a message for you.

words.meaning: Used to say who you are on the phone.

listen: Good afternoon, City Dental. How can I help you?
I am sorry, she is not at her desk. Can I take a message?
speak: Hello, could I speak to Mr Shah, please?
Could you ask him to call me back?

grammar.title: Object pronouns: me, him, her, us, them
grammar.rule: Subject pronouns do the action; object pronouns receive it.

quiz.prompt: Complete: Can you ask her to call ___ back?
quiz.explanation: After a verb, use the object pronoun.

options: I gave the file to he.
I gave the file to him.
I gave the file to his.
I gave he the file to.

lessons.title: Describing people

words.meaning: Behaving in a kind, open way.
Not speaking much, or making little noise.
words.example: He is quiet until you know him.
She is the funny one in the family.

listen: My sister is taller than me, with short dark hair and glasses.
He seems quiet at first, but he is very funny once he relaxes.
speak: My best friend is tall and very friendly.
He is quieter than his brother.

grammar.title: Adjective order and position
grammar.rule: Adjectives go before the noun, or after be. Never add -s to an adjective.

quiz.prompt: Which word describes someone who makes you laugh?

lessons.title: Comparing things

words.meaning: Of higher quality than something else.
words.example: This one is better than that one.

words.meaning: Of lower quality than something else.

words.example: The two flats are very similar.

words.meaning: The way two things are not the same.
words.example: The only difference is the price.
That is enough for two people.

listen: The blue one is cheaper, but the grey one is better quality.
They are very similar. The only real difference is the size.
speak: This one is better than the other.
The two are quite similar.

grammar.title: Comparatives with than
grammar.rule: Short adjectives add -er. Longer ones take more. Good and bad are irregular.

quiz.prompt: Complete: This phone is ___ than mine.
Which word means almost the same?

lessons.title: In the neighbourhood

words.example: The bakery is on the corner.
The bank is opposite the park.

words.meaning: In the space separating two things.
words.example: It is between the shop and the school.

words.meaning: A place to walk across a road safely.
words.example: Use the crossing by the lights.
The office is on the third floor.

listen: It is opposite the post office, between the pharmacy and the small cafe.
Take the second left, and it is the blue door on the corner.
speak: The shop is opposite the station.
It is between the bank and the cafe.

grammar.title: Prepositions of place
grammar.rule: Use in for enclosed spaces, on for surfaces and floors, at for points.

quiz.prompt: Complete: The office is ___ the second floor.
Which word means directly across from?

lessons.title: Likes and opinions

words.example: The film was long and boring.

words.meaning: Liked more than all the others.

listen: I thought it was amazing, honestly. My brother found it boring, so we disagree.
Do you mind if I open the window? Not at all, go ahead.
speak: I agree with you.
It is my favourite place in the city.

grammar.title: Verbs of liking plus -ing
grammar.rule: After like, love, hate, enjoy and do not mind, use the -ing form.
examples: I do not mind working late.

quiz.prompt: Complete: I do not mind ___ early.
